run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:02:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by HTTP 504 responses the proxy itself produced for POST /api/checkout: Envoy access logs show '504 UT response_timeout' with upstream 'frontend' and a 15000 ms upstream duration, and every sampled frontend-proxy 'ingress' error span is a 504 lasting ~15.0 s. That 15 s proxy timeout is shorter than the underlying failure: checkout's gRPC PlaceOrder blocks ~30 s while its HTTP POST to the email Service (http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation, ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080) fails with 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout', repeated in checkout's application log from 18:04:41Z onward. Email's own span throughput fell from ~40-74 spans per 2m earlier in the window to ~20-30 around 18:04 and 0 in the last returned sample, on both email pod instances, while both email pods stayed Running/Ready with 0 restarts, the Service Endpoints were correct, no OOM or crash event was observed, and CPU/memory stayed far below limits. The deepest supported origin is therefore the email Deployment's pods no longer accepting new TCP connections on port 8080 around 18:02-18:04; the in-container reason could not be verified because both email containers produced no log lines and define no readiness/liveness probe to test the listener.

claims.text: In the hour ending 2026-11-16T18:20:16Z, frontend-proxy recorded 220.95 error-status spans on operation 'ingress' against 19031.85 UNSET ingress spans, while its client operation 'router frontend egress' recorded 0 error-status spans. These are span counts, not request counts.

Each sampled frontend-proxy 'ingress' error span carries status {error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR} with a duration of about 15,001,000-15,002,000 us, and its child span 'router frontend egress' also lasts about 15,000,000 us with status tags {error="true", http.status_code="0"}.

frontend-proxy access logs show 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1' answered '504 UT response_timeout' with upstream 'frontend' and an upstream duration of 15000-15002 ms; every 504 line sampled in the 18:01-18:06 and 18:00-18:20 slices was on /api/checkout, while other paths in the same log were 200 via_upstream.

Trace 9d48a9b96ce8529d9cc951391a1769cd shows the chain load-generator POST -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' 504 (15.0 s) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (15.0 s) -> frontend 'POST' span of 15,000,276 us with http.status_code=200, while checkout work inside that request (prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart 93.6 ms, payment, shipping, cart) completed in milliseconds.

checkout recorded 100.94 error-status spans on operation 'HTTP POST' in the hour to 18:20:16Z; sampled error spans last ~30,000,000 us and carry otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout', and their parent checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' spans last ~29.7-30.4 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

ClusterIP 100.67.49.77 is the 'email' Service in namespace otel-demo (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080), and that Service's Endpoints contain both email pod IPs 100.96.2.7 (email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) and 100.96.3.218 (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w) on port 8080.

checkout's application log repeatedly reports 'failed to send order confirmation to "<user>@example.com": failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout', with entries from 18:04:41Z through at least 18:09:45Z.

The error burst begins in the same interval: frontend-proxy ingress error spans rise from 0-2.67 per 2m to 28, 41.33, 29.33 and 28 in the 2m intervals ending 18:04:16, 18:05:16, 18:06:16 and 18:07:16, and checkout 'HTTP POST' error spans first appear in the 2m interval ending 18:04:16 at 18.67.

email's own span throughput declines with the incident: 'POST /send_order_confirmation' (and 'send_email', 'sinatra.render_template') went from ~40-74 spans per 2m earlier in the window to ~20-30 around 18:04-18:05 and 0 in the last returned sample at 18:12:16; per-pod series show both exported_instance 3fb61602-10bf-4c1b-852c-d65334a985eb (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w) and 6a3edbee-fe4a-40ce-9e58-1591f36a2ad1 (email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) participating before the drop.

Both email pods are phase Running with Ready=True and restartCount 0, started 2026-11-16T17:28:50Z on two different nodes (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w on i-071e7666000f6d243, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn on i-0ba95c8c42c78df23); the email Deployment reports 2 desired, 2 ready and 2 available replicas; the container defines containerPort 8080 with no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe.

Resource exhaustion on email is not supported: container CPU usage stayed at ~0.0003-0.0035 cores against a 50m limit, memory working set stayed at ~51-52 MB against a 100Mi limit, and the container statuses show restartCount 0 with an empty lastState (no OOMKilled or terminated state).

An email crash or eviction is not supported: a query over otel-demo events returned an empty list for Warning-type and Unhealthy/Failed/Killing/BackOff/Evicted/OOM reasons among events visible between 17:47:02Z and 18:09:12Z, and the only email-pod events returned were Normal 'Updated' rows.

Rejected: a checkout-side general network or DNS failure. Checkout's other ClusterIP calls in the same trace completed successfully (cart GetCart/EmptyCart, product-catalog GetProduct, currency Convert, payment Charge, shipping /get-quote and /ship-order, all with rpc.grpc.status_code=0), and the failing message contains the already-resolved IP '100.67.49.77:8080', so only the email path failed.

Rejected: a node-level fault. The two email pods run on i-071e7666000f6d243 and i-0ba95c8c42c78df23, while other services co-located on those same nodes (cart, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment, checkout on i-071e7666000f6d243; currency, quote, shipping, valkey-cart on i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) served traffic successfully in the same trace.

Rejected: an email Service selector or port misconfiguration. The email Service selects opentelemetry.io/name=email on port 8080 targeting 8080, and its Endpoints list exactly the two running email pod IPs on port 8080, so the Service-to-pod wiring is consistent.

Primary hypothesis: the email application inside both email pods stopped accepting new TCP connections on port 8080 around 18:02-18:04, so checkout's connection attempt to the Service VIP was dropped and reported 'i/o timeout', email's served-span throughput fell toward zero, and each checkout PlaceOrder blocked ~30 s - longer than frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout, which produced the 504s that raised this alert.

Alternative not excluded: the packet path to the email Service VIP (kube-proxy/CNI/conntrack) rather than the email process is dropping connections. The Service object and Endpoints are correct, so this cannot be separated from an app-level listen/accept failure without node-level or in-pod evidence; email's declining served-span count fits an app-side accept failure better but does not exclude a VIP-path fault.

Add a readiness probe on the email container's 8080 port (and a liveness probe) so a pod that stops accepting connections leaves the email Service Endpoints instead of remaining Ready, and review whether checkout's dial/HTTP timeout path being longer than frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout is intended.

gaps: Why the email process stopped accepting connections is unknown: log reads for both email containers (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) returned status no_data with zero lines over 17:02:06-18:20:16, so no in-application error is available.

No readiness or liveness probe exists on the email container, so the Running/Ready pod state cannot be used as evidence that the port-8080 listener worked; no in-pod exec or connection test was possible in this Run.
The networkpolicies queries returned no_data (otel-demo namespace and cluster-wide), so the absence of a NetworkPolicy that could drop traffic to the email pods cannot be asserted.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was not found in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data for that rule name, and that tool has no time range), so the exact alert expression and the annotation's current value 0.2444444444444444 could not be independently reproduced.
RPC duration/count series filtered on rpc_grpc_status_code!="0" returned no_data, so gRPC-level error statistics could not be used and only status_code-labelled span metrics were available.
Range-query data for the span metrics used here ends around 18:12:16-18:16:16 (source_end_at/data_as_of), so email behaviour after ~18:12 and any recovery state are unknown.
The email container's previous-instance logs were unavailable (HTTP 400: previous terminated container not found), so pre-restart or earlier-instance application output could not be read.
Whether checkout, frontend-proxy or the load-generator fully recovered after 18:20:16 is not established; only the authorized window was examined.
next_steps: Inspect the email container's process state and listening sockets (for example an in-pod check of port 8080) to determine whether the process was blocked, backlog-saturated, or simply not bound.
Check kube-proxy/CNI and conntrack state on nodes i-071e7666000f6d243 and i-0ba95c8c42c78df23 for the email Service VIP 100.67.49.77 to rule in or out a VIP-path packet drop.
Add readiness/liveness probes to the email Deployment and review whether its 50m CPU limit is suitable for the Ruby/Sinatra workload.
Locate the alerting rule that fires RequestErrorRate for frontend-proxy, since it is not present in this Prometheus, to confirm its expression and threshold.
